- When sentiment turns negative or shows strong downward momentum (e.g., sentiment change < -0.33), model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days — cap forecast at +3–5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive but news volume drops (e.g., <3.0), model overestimates — reduce forecast by 2–5% to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment shows strong upward momentum (e.g., sentiment change > +0.67), model often fails to capture full rally — increase forecast by 1–3% beyond historical trend.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30d horizon when sentiment is volatile — add 1–2% buffer to forecast if sentiment variance > 0.5.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak (e.g., -0.67 → +0.67), model often lags — forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment shift.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome exceeds model by >5% in 3+ consecutive days, model is underestimating — adjust upward by 1–3% per day until trend stabilizes.
